correctness.rationale: Normal-coordinate metric and volume expansions are uniform in a convex normal ball. Radial Euclidean moment identities and tensor contractions give two independent fourth-order corrections whose sum is exactly -(n+8)Scal/[3(n+2)^2(n+4)]. The proof controls the normalization and O(r^5) remainder. Exact rational coefficient calculations (n=2..20) and independent Gauss–Legendre integration of exact spherical and hyperbolic geodesic distances in n=2,3 corroborate signs and constants; these finite checks are not substituted for the general proof.

originality.rationale: The explicit all-dimensional fourth-order coefficient for the normalized two-point intrinsic squared-distance statistic is not stated by the inspected sources. Veronelli computes local (n+1)-extent from optimal point configurations; Jauregui studies relative capacity; Hickok–Blumberg study ball-volume-growth estimators. Published-index searches of distance-moment/Riemannian-curvature aliases found no covering indexed statement. The distinction is implication-level rather than a title comparison; historical priority remains provisional.

value.rationale: Averaged two-point geodesic dispersion is a natural, unlabeled metric-measure observable distinct from radial ball volumes and extremal point configurations. The theorem supplies its exact universal first curvature coefficient and a direct scalar-curvature recovery formula for every smooth Riemannian manifold and every dimension at least two, linking inverse geometry and geometric sampling. Both the measure and metric corrections are essential, so this is not just relabeling the classical volume-growth coefficient; the formula does not claim finite-sample novelty or algorithmic superiority.
